photos.caption: Before sunrise off the coast of Florida

Hazy mid Atlantic morning

On mornings when the air is just cool enough and the water warm you can see a haze that feels like it envelops your eyes. Everything gets a glow to it like an oily camera lens.

Passing through a squall

You can see dense rain out on the horizon and sometimes you can avoid it but often enough there is nothing you can do but sail through.

Bird on the mast at sunrise

The boobies like to ride with us through the night while the albatrosses sleep with their wings locked in place.

Sunny morning

I imagine this is how the sun felt in The Stranger

Calm view from the bow

Sitting here reminded me of the Italian beaches on the Adriatic.
Lucas and Loriane on Dune du Pilat

Plana Cays from a distance

Uninhabited and where the last remaining Huita (a Bahamian rodent) colony was found.

Uninhibited cloud

Baudrillard called America's clouds unconfined, but any continent will confine its weather. Only at sea will you find a cloud which is bound by its will.

Following Cormorant

The birds must appreciate the clouds as well.
Approaching storm at the Panama Canal
Small lighthouse exiting the Panama Canal

Pacific Skipjack Tuna

This tuna was caught from a school of tens of thousands. They churn the surface while eating, replicating a wind torn sea. This school was nearly a mile long.

Dolphins 150 miles off Costa Rica

Good luck for sailors.

Boobies gathered on the mast

They cover our deck with shit and can't be scared away.
Nazca Booby above a Brown Booby in the early hours

Full moon through binoculars

It's incredible how the moon can light up the sea. Its easy to forget that the sun hasn't risen when the moon reflects against every wave.
The moon lighting up the sky behind a cloud

Birds hunting the flying fish

If you zoom in you can see the fish above the water.
View from the bridge during a squall

Ile Clipperton lit by the moon

This island is now a French territory but it was once Mexican. In the early 20th century a mad lighthouse keeper kept a group of women captive on the island until they killed him with a hammer and escaped via canoe to a US Navy ship. It's now uninhabited.
